intelligence.essence: A change in evidence eligibility must trigger a change in the right to use a conclusion — not automatic destruction of the knowledge that carried it. Preserve history. Recompute current qualification. Invalidate stale authority-bearing projections. Refresh only what changed. Keep independently supported conclusions available. The most important distinction is between discoverability and certifiability: a source may remain discoverable for research, debugging, and learning while no longer permitted to certify an outcome or justify consequential execution. A Smart Note can remain historically accurate while one claim loses certification; an index can point to it without advertising it as verified; a successor package can preserve what earlier Nayas believed without letting a new Naya inherit outdated proof. NayaNET reports: 'One evidence source lost certification eligibility. Three qualifications required reassessment. One was suspended, one was narrowed, one was independently requalified. Historical notes remain preserved, search shows current standing, successor packages cannot reuse stale proof.'
intelligence.falsifier: A stale cached summary served as current verified intelligence; a successor package's old qualification reused as fresh authority; a refreshed projection silently rewriting history as though always updated; an older cache refresh overwriting a newer revocation; the eligible_independent_evidence field asserting eligibility for an ineligible source; discoverability removal used as a substitute for certifiability restriction.

human_view.meaning: When evidence goes bad, you don't burn the library — you update the card catalog. Every summary, note, index entry, and handoff package carries a list of exactly which claims it depends on and which version of the truth it was built from. When a claim's standing changes, only the affected passages get annotated or regenerated — the rest stays. And there's a bouncer at the door: even if a cached page hasn't been redrawn yet, the system checks the current standing before serving it as verified. Old packages are sealed time capsules with a mandatory 'check what's still true' step before anything gets reused. History stays readable; only the authority to act on it expires.

intelligence.learning_lesson: This is the projection half of the correction discipline: SN-0783 recomputes the claims; this invalidates what the claims were PROJECTED into. Together with the read-time qualification gate, they close the last stale-authority hole: recomputation without invalidation leaves yesterday's certificates circulating; invalidation without recomputation leaves nothing to replace them with. The concrete build_successor_package() defect is the pattern made flesh — a field NAMED eligible that was never filtered — and its repair (historical vs currently-eligible refs) is the template for every projection surface.

intelligence.measurement_contract: Ten regression tests: three-claim summary, one loses qualification → only affected text changes; note copies obsolete receipt → preserved as history, not current proof; index points to ineligible source → discoverability retained, certification restricted; E1 ineligible + E2 suffices → stays qualified; shared-origin false independence → rejected; staging survives → broad claim downgraded; old successor reopened → current qualification reconstructed; source changes mid-planning → stale proof cannot authorize commitment; unknown contamination scope → affected held, unrelated unaffected; two refresh jobs race → older revision never overwrites newer (generation-bound compare-and-swap; failed stale write retained as diagnostic). Four-surface cascade fixture: E1 ineligible → A loses, B survives via E2, C downgrades to staging → summaries/notes/indexes/successors reconcile; stale qualifications unusable; history reconstructable; cold successor reaches same verdict.

naya_view.directive: Give every projection a manifest: claim dependencies with revisions and receipts, qualification snapshot generation, projection status, historical-content-preserved flag. Map each recomputation verdict to its cache action. Run the two-phase invalidation: commit eligibility change → dependency closure → recompute → publish new generation → refresh affected projections → independently reconcile. Gate every served projection at read time against current qualification. Apply per-surface policies; never silently rewrite history. Repair the successor-package eligibility field split. Never let a stale refresh overwrite a newer revocation.

simple_view.meaning: Update the card catalog, not the library. Old pages stay readable; only the permission to act on them expires — and the bouncer checks at the door.
